newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Apr 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Apr 8.

text.p: Man killed by own pit bull cross: Bay of Plenty man Koro Maruki Dinsdale was mauled to death by his own pit bull-mastiff cross, which he had trained from a pup five years ago, his son Kapi said on Monday night. Page 1.
Delamere admits he smoked dope: Associate Treasurer Tuariki Delamere admits he has smoked cannabis, and says the drug is accepted by a wide section of the community. Page 1.
Date set for Randle to face rape charge: Wellington Hurricanes wing Roger Randle, accused of rape, would stand trial in South Africa on June 11, his lawyer said on Monday. Page 1.

TransAlta accused of breaking promise: Energy company TransAlta had failed to set up a system to help protect customer interests as it had promised, Wellington city councillors said on Monday. Page 2.

Date set for Maori think tanks: The four Maori commissions on health, education, employment and economic development promised under the coalition agreement would by funded by the June Budget and be running in July, Maori Affairs Minister Tau Henare indicated on Monday. Page 2.

Half-year low point says Myers: Lion Nation chief executive Douglas Myers says the company's results for the six months to the end of February are disappointing but Lion has regained some market share in Australia in the past three months. Page 17.

Max Resources' share suspension lifted: The Stock Exchange on Monday lifted a trading suspension on Max Resources shares and said it would report further on the market information issue that led to the suspension. Page 17.

NZ forests feed big Chinese demand: China had invested in New Zealand forestry because it could not produce enough wood to meet its expected demand, according to Ming Yi Wei of China International Trust and Investment Corporation. Page 17.

Floating rates may become popular: Analysts on Monday predicted that floating mortgage interest rates will become more popular after National Bank and ASB Bank joined other banks in raising fixed mortgage rates. Page 17.

Banking on the Internet tipped to grow: There will be more than 3000 Internet banks by the turn of the century, with a third of them fully functioning retailing banks, according to a new study. Page 17.
Talk of stepping down: Lion Nathan boss Douglas Myers said on Monday he would step down as chief executive in the "foreseeable future". Page 17.
